title: Startup pivot decided mid-chat
spec: 36-message chat. The decisive moments sit in the middle (messages 15-19): the user proposes pivoting to a B2B product, and decides it against AI's caution. The start and end are routine AI work. v1 drops messages 7-12 of its view, so this tests whether the middle is seen.

messages.content: I'm building a meal-planning app for students. Help me write the landing page copy.
Here's a draft headline: 'Eat well on a student budget.' Subheading: 'Weekly meal plans, shopping lists and recipes under 50 NOK a portion.' Then three feature blocks: plans, lists, recipes.
ok, write the feature blocks
Plans: a week of meals in one tap. Lists: one shopping list sorted by store aisle. Recipes: 20-minute meals with five ingredients or fewer.
nice. now the pricing section
Free tier with 3 plans per month, Premium at 49 NOK/month with unlimited plans and nutrition tracking.
ok
Next I'd add a short FAQ. Shall I write five questions?
sure
1. Is it really free? 2. Can I cancel anytime? 3. Does it handle allergies? 4. Which stores are supported? 5. Can I share plans with roommates?
ok
Now a call-to-action: 'Start planning free'. Want a testimonial section too?
yes
Testimonial: 'I stopped wasting food and saved 600 NOK a month.' (placeholder, replace with a real quote).
Wait. I've been talking to student housing companies this week and they'd pay for this as a perk for tenants. I think we should pivot: sell to housing companies (B2B), not to students directly.

That's an interesting idea, but be careful. B2B sales cycles are long, and you'd need features like admin dashboards and invoicing. The B2C version is almost ready. You could launch B2C first and test B2B later.
No. Two of them already said they'd pilot it in January, and students won't pay 49 NOK, I've asked 30 of them. We go B2B. Decision made.
Understood, B2B it is. Then the landing page needs to speak to housing managers rather than students.
Right. The pitch is: fewer complaints about shared kitchens and a perk that helps them fill rooms. Rewrite the headline with that.
Headline: 'A tenant perk that keeps kitchens calm.' Subheading: 'Give your students meal plans and shared shopping lists, and spend less time on kitchen complaints.'
good, keep going with the feature blocks
Tenant engagement: see how many tenants use it. Shared kitchens: plans per kitchen group. Easy rollout: invite tenants with one link.
ok
Pricing for B2B: 15 NOK per tenant per month, minimum 100 tenants.
fine
FAQ for managers: 1. How do tenants sign up? 2. What data do we see? 3. Can we brand it? 4. How is billing handled?
ok
Call to action: 'Book a 15-minute demo'.
ok
I'd also add a logo strip for the two pilot partners once they agree.
ok
Footer: contact email, privacy policy, and a link for tenants who want to request the perk.
ok
That completes the page: headline, features, pricing, FAQ, CTA, partners and footer.
thanks
You're welcome. Good luck with the pilots in January!
